targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing digital-employee runtimes with delegated workers and resource limits
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands agent delegation, budgets, checkpoints and lifecycle control.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Per-worker accounting can let nested delegation hide the total cost of one authorized objective, while a root total alone can erase which worker caused the spend.

whyNow: A same-day merged OpenAI Codex maintainer change demonstrates shared root-goal token accounting across nested workers, idle progress, goal replacement, checkpoint races and an unloaded intermediate parent.

externalHook.description: Nested workers publish usage into a shared root accumulator without losing worker-level origin.

coreProposition: Delegated resource consumption should preserve worker-level origin evidence while charging the inherited budget to the root objective that authorized the work; accurate shared-root accounting closes a demonstrated delegation escape but does not itself prove immediate cancellation, generalized quotas or exactly-once enforcement.

originalValue.description: Separates the factual origin of resource use from the governance identity that owns the inherited budget, then separates accounting truth from enforcement proof.

readerTakeaway: Track both descendant origin and root-objective budget ownership; treat limit detection, admission denial and cancellation as separate evidenced transitions.

supported: The merged implementation routes descendant token increments into shared root accounting.
The demonstrated mechanism covers active and idle progress, goal replacement, checkpoint concurrency and an unloaded intermediate parent.
Combined root and descendant token usage can move the root goal into a budget-limited state.
unsupported: Generalized quotas for money, time, memory, network or tool calls
Distributed exactly-once charging or cross-host enforcement
uncertain: The safest enforcement boundary after budget exhaustion
The durable receipt needed across process crashes and objective migration

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general delegated-resource governance pattern without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The source-level change and regression coverage support a concrete accounting mechanism, an original dual-identity interpretation and a clear enforcement boundary.
